title: World Literature
description: Famous novels, plays and poems and the writers behind them

questions.question: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
questions.explanation: Jane Austen published 'Pride and Prejudice' in 1813. It follows Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play features the line 'To be, or not to be'?
questions.explanation: The line opens Prince Hamlet's famous soliloquy in Act 3, Scene 1 of 'Hamlet'.

questions.question: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?
questions.explanation: Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez published it in 1967. It is a landmark of magical realism.

questions.question: Which novel begins with the line 'Call me Ishmael'?
choices: The Old Man and the Sea
questions.explanation: Herman Melville's 'Moby-Dick' (1851) opens with Ishmael introducing himself before joining Captain Ahab's whaling voyage.

questions.question: Who wrote the dystopian novel '1984'?
questions.explanation: George Orwell published '1984' in 1949. Huxley wrote 'Brave New World' and Bradbury wrote 'Fahrenheit 451'.

questions.question: Which ancient Greek epic follows Odysseus's journey home after the Trojan War?
questions.explanation: Homer's 'Odyssey' tells of Odysseus's ten-year voyage home to Ithaca. The 'Iliad' covers the war itself, and the 'Aeneid' is Virgil's Latin epic.

questions.question: Who wrote 'War and Peace'?
questions.explanation: Leo Tolstoy wrote 'War and Peace', set during the Napoleonic invasion of Russia. Dostoevsky wrote 'Crime and Punishment'.

questions.question: In 'Don Quixote', what does the hero mistake for giants?
questions.explanation: Don Quixote charges at windmills believing they are giants, the origin of the phrase 'tilting at windmills'. The novel is by Miguel de Cervantes.

questions.question: Who wrote 'Things Fall Apart'?
questions.explanation: Nigerian author Chinua Achebe published 'Things Fall Apart' in 1958. It follows Okonkwo and the impact of colonialism on Igbo society.

questions.question: Which author created the detective Hercule Poirot?
questions.explanation: Agatha Christie introduced the Belgian detective Hercule Poirot in 'The Mysterious Affair at Styles' (1920). Conan Doyle created Sherlock Holmes.
